feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: How abuse in some of Tennessee's juvenile prisons remained under wraps
entry.summary: Employees at a group of privately-run juvenile detention facilities across Tennessee failed to report suspected physical and sexual abuse to the state, and were allegedly discouraged from calling 911.

entry.title: Questions remain after grand jury declines indictment in Nolan Wells' death
entry.summary: The Black Mississippi teen's family questions whether his race contributed to his July 4th death on an island off the Mississippi coast.

entry.title: Girl accuses Braden Peters, social media influencer known as 'Clavicular,' of rape
entry.summary: The allegations claim Braden Peters, also known as Clavicular, had non-consensual sex with the 17-year-old female victim after plying her with alcohol. Peters' representative denies the charges.

entry.title: White House launches 'Trump TV' after ban on major news outlets
entry.summary: Days after President Trump barred reporters from three major news outlets from the White House, the administration has launched a 24/7 YouTube channel promising to put its "biggest moments all in one place."

entry.title: Trump's D.C. arch is now a military complex. Here's how that complicates things
entry.summary: The future of Trump's D.C. arch was already fraught. Then he rebranded it as a military complex. Experts say that only raises more legal and logistical questions.

entry.title: A journalist once barred from the White House says this media ban is different
entry.summary: Jim Acosta has already been through a White House press-pass fight. Now, three news organizations are barred, and he says the press is showing solidarity that should have come sooner.

entry.title: New DNA analysis adds evidence Jefferson fathered children with Sally Hemings
entry.summary: A lock of hair, 15 years of sleuthing and a 200-year-old question. In History by a Hair, Smithsonian Institution scholar Richard Kurin follows the DNA trail back to Thomas Jefferson.

entry.title: How unarmed 911 teams are reshaping public safety in nearly 100 cities
entry.summary: Alternative response programs, where mental health clinicians respond to 911 calls instead of police, have proliferated since George Floyd's murder. What does it take to do this work well?

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: CNN, MSNOW and Politico file lawsuit after White House ban, Trump to address world leaders at U.N. General Assembly, Paramount settles lawsuit with states over Warner Bros. Discovery merger.

entry.title: California Attorney General Bonta says states made demands in Paramount-Warner deal
entry.summary: The settlement brings a two-month legal fight over Paramount's Warner Bros. Discovery takeover closer to an end.
